title: feat(editor): wheel-button zoom and "zoom with scroll wheel" preference
body:
## Summary

Two wheel-navigation features, plus what fell out of building them.

- **Zoom by scrolling with the wheel (middle) button held down.** Same zoom as ctrl/cmd+wheel, anchored on the pointer. It wins over the modifiers and over the drag-pan the button itself starts, so a wheel-button pan can be zoomed one-handed without reaching for a key. Read off `event.buttons`, no extra state.
- **Input device preference** (`appState.inputDevice`: `"auto" | "mouse" | "trackpad"`, default `"auto"`, persisted to browser storage). A trackpad has a 2D pan gesture and a separate pinch (delivered as ctrl+wheel); a mouse has one notched axis and no pinch. With `"trackpad"` a plain wheel pans and ctrl/cmd+wheel zooms, as before; with `"mouse"` a plain wheel zooms and ctrl/cmd+wheel pans vertically instead, while shift+wheel keeps panning horizontally, a horizontal-only wheel (tilt wheel, sideways two-finger scroll) pans sideways, and the wheel-button zoom is unaffected. `"auto"` is reserved for detecting the device from the wheel events and resolves to `"trackpad"` through `resolveInputDevice()` until that exists. The preferences submenu gets a Trackpad / Mouse radio (also exported as `MainMenu.DefaultItems.Preferences.InputDevice`) that shows what `"auto"` resolves to.
- **Wheel handling extracted** from `App.tsx` into `App.wheel.ts` (`AppWheel`), in the same shape as the other `App.*` helpers.
- **Zoom-during-pan consistency.** Zooming mid-pan exposed three ways the point grabbed by the pan drifted from under the cursor, compounding per tick: the drag-pan wrote its scroll from `this.state` as a plain object and overwrote a zoom queued in the same React flush; a pointer move still waiting for its animation frame landed after the zoom; and the zoom updater read the anchor position when React evaluated it rather than when the wheel fired. All three are fixed, each pinned by a regression test. The same kind of stale read in `viewport.translate` made a pan queued behind a zoom tick count as a zoom and hard-clamp the rubberband overscroll to zero; `translate` is now a single updater that compares against the state it applies to. Zoom ticks that land on the zoom they started from (at the zoom limits) no longer flip the bitmap-cache flag and redraw the scene.
- **Zoom bitmap cache kept across pan frames.** `viewport.translate` cleared `shouldCacheIgnoreZoom` on every call, so every pan frame between two zoom ticks re-rasterized all elements at the in-progress zoom. With 1,200 rough shapes on screen, a 12-tick zoom with the pointer moving regenerated ~10k bitmaps with frames up to 283 ms; after the change it regenerates none and stays under 33 ms. The reset now happens only when a gesture interrupts an animated `setViewport`.
- **Wheel over a frame label is handled once.** The label's React `onWheel` duplicated the container's native listener, so wheel input over labels panned and zoomed twice per tick (pre-existing).

## Testing

- New `wheel.test.tsx` (11 tests) and two new cases in `scrollConstraints.test.tsx`; the full suite passes.
- Verified in Chrome with real pointer and wheel events: no drift of the grabbed point across ten interleaved move-and-zoom cycles, the mouse mode's modifier behavior, the bitmap-regeneration counts above, and single-step handling over frame labels.

fable 5.1
